![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/91e8b39eb1bf181ceaf5b33b25fbb5ed0fa3ca7f7c1f0bb830c3337f142eb1dd.png)

Evaluate the triple integral 
${∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,dV$
over the region $R,$ shown above.

*Hint: All surfaces, except for the top one, are parallel to the corresponding coordinate planes.*
feedback.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/5c8b476bceea5225cd230bd6e881706269b6eeda415503266e96e6e3c676b237.png)

 

Notice that our solid can be written as the type I region

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(x,y)\in D,\,\,0\le z\le 1+y},
$$

where

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2}
$$

is the projection of $R$ onto the $xy$-plane, shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062541/assets/31f2ff96afa1248427c1a6dd5074c47190c70983d7c0d5dfdd3def8bd883aef8.png)

Hence, we can express the region $R$ as

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 2,\,\,0\le z\le 1+y}
$$

As a result, by writing down our triple integral as a repeated integral, we obtain

$$
{∭}_{R}{z}^{2}\,\text{d}V={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+y}{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx.
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $z$, treating $x$ and $y$ as constants: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{1+y}{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{1+y}{z}^{2}\,dz]dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}{[\frac{{z}^{3}}{3}]}_{z=0}^{z=1+y}\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{(1+y)^{3}}{3}\,dy\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y$, treating $x$ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{(1+y)^{3}}{3}\,dy\,dx & ={\int }_{0}^{3}[{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{(1+y)^{3}}{3}\,dy]dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}{[\frac{(1+y)^{4}}{12}]}_{y=0}^{y=2}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{1}{12}(81-1)\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{20}{3}\,dx\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{3}\frac{20}{3}\,dx & ={[\frac{20}{3}x]}_{x=0}^{x=3} \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$
